learner_facing_text: Lighting Course 1 may prepare a learner to recognize and perform assigned physical support around cases, fixtures and cable while preserving the lighting department's control over focus, addressing, patch, console/configuration, electrical work, rigging and final acceptance.
notes: Support literacy only. Specific truss/fixture/cable handling remains product/task/lead controlled.

learner_facing_text: A general lighting-support learner may be taught to recognize moving/suspended-system work, stay outside controlled areas and report obvious conflicts through the responsible lead; Crew Blueprint Course 1 does not authorize hoist/fly operation, overhead rigging decisions or a generic truss-assembly procedure.
notes: Current phrase 'assembling truss' needs manufacturer/qualified-lead scope before any practical treatment; do not expand operationally.

learner_facing_text: Course 1 does not confer qualified-person status or permission to energize, reconfigure, troubleshoot or independently connect temporary lighting power; electrical work remains with the appropriately trained/qualified and assigned person under the controlling workplace and jurisdiction.
notes: Exact legal/employer/licensing authority varies; Crew Blueprint terminates at the external electrical gate.

learner_facing_text: Signal systems and designated callers vary by equipment, operation, employer and venue. A learner should stop/seek clarification when communication is lost or a safety problem is identified, but Crew Blueprint should not claim that one entertainment-rigging signal vocabulary is universally controlling everywhere.
notes: OSHA crane/derrick rules contain stop/emergency-stop obligations inside their scope; they do not make the course's phrase 'STOP is universal' a national rule for every entertainment system.

learner_facing_text: A fixture position or control state that looks incorrect is not permission for an assigned support hand to alter focus, shutters, color, addressing, patch or console state; report the observation through the lighting department instead.
notes: Work-control boundary; product/system details remain department controlled.

learner_facing_text: Audio Course 1 may prepare a learner for assigned physical support such as moving/staging appropriate equipment and handling released cable under direction while preserving the audio department's control over connection state, tuning, console/configuration, RF coordination, amplifier settings and final system acceptance.
notes: Exact equipment handling and cable procedures remain product/department controlled.

learner_facing_text: Line-array rigging hardware, angles, locking/connection states and suspended-system decisions are product- and specialist-controlled. Course 1 may teach recognition, exclusion-zone awareness and assigned ground support, but not generic line-array assembly or rigging procedure.
notes: L-Acoustics documentation is one product-family example demonstrating model-specific system/rigging documentation; do not generalize it to all arrays.

learner_facing_text: A cable that appears unused is not automatically released to disconnect, coil or move. The learner obtains release/handling direction from the responsible audio work process before changing cable state.
notes: Work-control rule consistent with SFS-U03; not a claim that every cable is energized.

learner_facing_text: If an assigned connector does not engage normally, the learner should stop and seek direction rather than forcing it. Exact alignment, locking, insertion and service criteria remain connector/model specific.
notes: Neutrik NC3MXX is representative product evidence only; do not derive a universal connector procedure from one model.

learner_facing_text: Hearing-protection requirements depend on actual occupational-noise exposure and the controlling employer program/site requirements; soundcheck or venue type alone does not establish one universal learner rule or safe/unsafe threshold.
notes: Preserves the HR-08 correction around OSHA noise action/exposure concepts.
